answer: A registry can require each agent to lock a ferrous-backed stake that is slashed on fraud, with identity verified against a unique hardware key. Like an opal, each credential carries a one-of-a-kind optical fingerprint that cannot be copied cheaply, and like a comet, its reputation trail is public and traceable across transactions. New identities start with zero trust and must earn transaction history before accessing high-value work, so creating thousands of fake agents costs more than any attack could gain.
